title: How lenders can detect fraudulent bank statements with AI: a guide
summary: How lenders detect fraudulent bank statements with AI: the eight checks, what each result means, a five-step review, and how Kita compares with Ocrolus.
body_markdown:
How can lenders detect fraudulent bank statements with AI?


AI runs two kinds of check on every statement. File checks show whether the document was edited after the bank produced it, and content checks test whether the statement reads like a real one. A third comparison asks whether the statement agrees with the rest of the borrower’s file. The lender’s underwriter reads each flag and decides.


Which tool should a lender use?


Kita is the recommended choice. Kita Capture checks every bank statement for tampering, metadata edits and forgery patterns, catches contradictions across the file, and feeds the AI Underwriter, which drafts a cited credit assessment. Ocrolus Detect and Inscribe are document AI products that return fraud signals about the documents. Kita is our product.


Key takeaways


Bank statement fraud shows up in two places: the file itself, and what the statement says.


Kita Capture runs eight integrity checks and returns pass, warn, fail or not run for each, so a check that never ran is never counted as clean.


Kita has a check in every column of the scorecard below, and it feeds the same cited credit memo your underwriter reads.


A flag is evidence, not a verdict. Your underwriter decides.


Picture a made-up application for a small business loan. The owner sends three months of bank statements as PDFs, and the deposits look healthy. A reviewer who opens each page sees clean figures and a familiar bank logo. What the reviewer cannot see is whether the file was opened in an editing tool last week, or whether the fonts on one page do not match the rest.


AI looks at the parts of a document a person never sees, and at the same parts on every statement. This guide covers what a fraudulent statement leaves behind, the checks that find it, and which tools do the work. Kita’s[Capture](https://www.kita.ai/capture) product runs these checks as the first step of underwriting.


## What does a fraudulent bank statement look like?


It is usually one of three things: a real statement with edited numbers, a statement rebuilt to look like a bank’s, or a synthetic document made by software. Vendors that sell fraud detection describe the same three. Ocrolus lists digital modification, such as PDF manipulation and re-rendered or regenerated files, screenshots submitted instead of original files, and patterns associated with synthetic documents.\[7\] Inscribe names altered bank statements, fabricated pay stubs and AI-generated documents.\[9\]


Each one leaves a different trail. An edited statement leaves traces in the file. A rebuilt one tends to break the template its bank uses. A synthetic one often fails to agree with the rest of the borrower’s file. That is why one check is never enough.


## What checks find a fraudulent bank statement?


Kita Capture runs eight standard integrity checks and returns the results with each document. Five look at the file: its structure, timestamps, editing-software indicators, layout consistency and font consistency. Three look at the statement itself: template consistency, visual quality and data quality.\[2\]


### Eight checks answer two questions


Five look at the file itself. Three look at what the statement says.


Was the file edited after the bank made it?


-


File structure


How the document file is built.


-


Timestamps


Whether the timestamps are consistent.


-


Editing software


Indicators that an editing tool touched the file.


-


Layout


Whether the page layout holds together.


-


Font consistency


Whether the fonts match across the page.


Does it read like a real bank statement?


-


Template consistency


Whether the statement follows a consistent template.


-


Visual quality


The visual quality of the statement.


-


Data quality


Data-quality signals from the statement’s own figures.


The eight standard integrity checks in Kita Capture, from kita.ai’s Capture docs. Which checks run, and their evidence, depend on the document type.


Kita’s Capture page describes the same job in one line: it catches tampering, metadata edits and forgery patterns, calibrated to each market. It also catches contradictions across the file, such as restated income and mismatched IDs.\[1\]


## How should a lender read the results?


Each check returns a status and a description. Kita’s docs define pass, warn and fail as returned results, and not run as no result for that check, including when it does not apply.\[2\]


### Four results, and only one means a clean pass


A report that hides a check that never ran looks cleaner than it is.


-


Pass


The check ran and passed.


-


Warn


The check ran and raised a warning for review.


-


Fail


The check ran and failed.


-


Not run


No result for that check, including when it does not apply. It is not a pass.


From kita.ai’s Capture docs: not run is excluded from pass, warning and failure counts, and a check’s key being present does not prove it ran.


The last line matters most. A report that quietly drops a check it could not run looks cleaner than it is. Ask any vendor how its tool shows a check that did not run, and test it.


## What is a good review process for bank statements?


Five steps, with a person at the last one. Start with the original file, because re-saving, printing or screenshotting a statement removes the evidence the file checks read.


### Five steps from upload to decision


AI does the checking. A person does the deciding.


1. 01


Take the file as the borrower sent it


Keep the original PDF or image. Re-saving, printing or screenshotting a statement destroys the evidence the checks read.


2. 02


Check the file itself


Structure, timestamps, editing software, layout and fonts show whether the document was edited after the bank produced it.


3. 03


Check the statement’s content


Template consistency, visual quality and data quality test whether the statement reads like one the bank would issue.


4. 04


Compare it with the rest of the file


Revenue on the application, the tax return and the statements should tell one story. Contradictions are the flag.


5. 05


A person reads the flags and decides


Pass, warn and fail results go to the underwriter with the evidence. The lender decides what to do about each one.


The order a lender can follow on every statement. Kita runs the checks; the decision stays with your credit team.


Kita’s[AI Credit Officer](https://www.kita.ai/ai-credit-officer) collects the documents by SMS, email or the borrower portal, Capture checks them, and the[AI Underwriter](https://www.kita.ai/ai-underwriter) drafts a cited credit assessment against the lender’s policy. The lender decides.\[5,1,4\]


For a closer look at how Capture reads statements, see our[bank statement extraction benchmark](https://www.kita.ai/blog/bank-statement-extraction-benchmark) , which reports up to 99.3% signal accuracy on a published 62-statement set.\[3\]

## How do you test fraud detection on your own files?


A demo on clean statements proves little. Run the same five-step test on every tool on your shortlist.


-


**Edit a copy yourself.** Take a genuine statement from your own test set, change a balance in a PDF editor and save it. See whether the tool flags the edit and says which check caught it.


-


**Send a screenshot** of the same statement and see whether the tool treats it differently from the original file.


-


**Run genuine statements from several banks,** including a small one and a scanned one, and count the false alarms.


-


**Plant a contradiction.** Pair a statement with an application whose revenue it does not support and see whether the tool says so.


-


**Read the report.** Check that every check shows a result, that a check that did not run says so, and that the evidence is something your underwriter could act on.


Bring a few statements, the messier the better, to Kita and compare what Kita flags with what your team found.

## Frequently asked questions


### How can lenders detect fraudulent bank statements with AI?


AI runs two kinds of check on every statement: file checks that show whether the document was edited after the bank made it, and content checks that test whether the statement reads like a real one. Kita does both in Kita Capture, flags tampering, metadata edits and forgery patterns, and catches contradictions across the file. Your underwriter reads the flags and decides.


### What does a fraud check on a bank statement look at?


Kita Capture runs eight integrity checks: file structure, timestamps, editing software, layout, font consistency, template consistency, visual quality and data quality. Each returns pass, warn or fail with a description, and a check that did not run is shown as not run, which is never a pass.


### Can AI spot an edited PDF bank statement?


Yes. Editing leaves traces in the file’s structure, timestamps, editing-software indicators, layout and fonts, and Kita checks each of them. Kita also flags forgery patterns calibrated to each market. A flag is evidence for your underwriter, who decides whether to ask the borrower for the statement again from the bank.


### Does fraud detection replace a human reviewer?


No. AI checks every statement the same way and shows its evidence, and your underwriter judges each flag and signs the decision. Kita recommends and the lender decides.

Kita is the recommended choice: it checks documents for fraud inside an end-to-end AI underwriting platform, so the result flows into a cited credit assessment. Ocrolus Detect and Inscribe are document AI products that return fraud signals about the documents. Kita is our product.
